headline: Shallow M7.7 earthquake under the Azuero Peninsula. Damage reported across Coclé, Veraguas, Los Santos and Herrera; no official casualty figures yet.
key_points: No authority has confirmed any deaths as of 20:30 UTC (15:30 local). SINAPROC director Omar Smith reported "several injured" without a figure; at least 1 injured at Penonomé market.

Heaviest documented building damage is in Penonomé (Coclé), ~110 km from the epicentre: partial collapse of Hotel Dos Continentes, cathedral tower fell, Gobernación wall collapsed, hospital patients evacuated.

Near the epicentre (southern Azuero): El Sitio hostel at Playa Venao collapsed — locals told La Prensa people were trapped, but local authorities say the damaged tourist buildings in Pedasí were unoccupied; no official confirmation of anyone trapped. Telemetro describes Cambutal/Tonosí as the most affected area; houses collapsed near Tonosí.

Veraguas: damage to Santiago cathedral, municipal building, bus terminal and Policlínica Horacio Díaz Gómez; Atalaya basilica tower partly collapsed; Soná fire station damaged; road to Torio (Mariato) ruptured.
Strong aftershock sequence: IGC-UP reports 46 aftershocks so far, the largest about M6.4–6.5 (IGC figures vary); largest in the USGS catalogue is M5.8.

Modelled estimates: USGS PAGER red alert for economic losses (median ~US$1.7 bn; 0–9% of GDP) and yellow for fatalities (most likely 10–100). ~490,000 people in very strong shaking (MMI VII+) per USGS PAGER; this dashboard's own estimate is ~426,000.

areas.text: Partial collapse of Hotel Dos Continentes; San Juan Bautista cathedral tower fell onto a car; Gobernación wall collapsed; market damaged (1 injured); Hospital Aquilino Tejeira cracked and evacuated; Iguana Mall damaged.
Described as the most affected area by Telemetro; partial collapse of a hotel and adjoining houses; road damage. Closest towns to the epicentre; strongest modelled shaking (MMI VIII–IX).
El Sitio hostel collapsed. Locals told La Prensa people were trapped, but local authorities say the damaged tourist buildings in Pedasí were unoccupied. No official confirmation of anyone trapped.
Cathedral and municipal building damaged (partial roof collapse); bus terminal and Policlínica Horacio Díaz Gómez damaged.
Soná fire station damaged; road to Torio (Mariato) split with vertical offsets; Santiago–Arenas road cut.
Part of the Basílica Menor tower collapsed.

areas.area: Chitré, Las Minas & La Villa, Herrera/Los Santos
areas.text: SINAPROC reports damage in Chitré (no details); cracked homes in Las Minas; San Atanasio church bell tower cracked in La Villa de Los Santos. Few images yet — information gap.
Broken windows on Calle 50 and Paitilla; hospitals evacuated as a precaution; Metro lines 1 and 2 suspended; Tocumen airport closed.

services.text: Outages in six provinces (Chiriquí, Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas, Coclé, part of Panamá Oeste); 17 circuits restored in Colón.
Chilibre treatment plant (serves most of Panama City & San Miguelito) at 20% capacity.
Widespread mobile and internet failures across several operators.
Tocumen International closed and evacuated; flights diverted to Barranquilla, Cartagena, Bogotá, San José, Managua and Panamá Pacífico.
Road to Torio (Mariato) ruptured; Santiago–Arenas road cut; damage around Cambutal.
Operating normally; ACP denied rumours of damage to Agua Clara locks.
Classes suspended nationwide; University of Panama closed; public offices closed by presidential order.
PTWC initially warned of 1–3 m waves on Panama's coasts; later no Pacific-wide threat. No tsunami damage reported.

upcoming: Press conference by Minister Montalvo and SINAPROC announced by President Mulino — figures on this page will be updated as soon as official numbers are published.
